title: Start Here
text:
Overview
This learning lab follows the complete workflow from REDCap API access through secure data extraction.


1. Enable API access
Request a project-specific REDCap API token.


2. Store the token securely
Keep credentials outside the code and project directory.


3. Call REDCap
Use the R or SAS example to retrieve the report.


4. Reuse and automate
Save unchanged extracts to DataRaw and support repeatable runs.








NoteDesign principle



Credentials stay separate from the code and extracted data.




Training files
Complete R and SAS programs are available on the Code & Downloads page. Code can be copied directly from the site or downloaded as the original .R and .sas files.

R extraction: Code/01_get_redcap_R.R
R automation: Code/02_schedule.R
SAS extraction: Code/01_get_redcap_sas.sas

title: Key Terms
text:
Key terms
This page will contain the key terms used throughout the REDCap API training.

title: 1. Get Token
text:
In the appropriate REDCap project, select API from the Applications section of the left sidebar.



Select Obtain API token for the project.
images/img_api_request_token.png{fig-alt=“REDCap API token request screen”}






ImportantToken handling




Do not share the token with other people.
Do not include the token in screenshots.
Do not place the token in R or SAS code.
Do not commit the token to Git.
When the project is complete, the token can be deleted and generated again later if needed.

title: 2. Store Securely
text:
The REDCap URI and API token should be stored outside the R or SAS program and outside the project directory.


Create the REDCap URI and project-specific token under Windows User variables.

redcap_uri → REDCap API web address
token_xxx → project-specific REDCap token




Windows User Environment Variables setup








Note



After adding or changing environment variables, completely close and reopen R, Positron, RStudio, or SAS before testing them.




R
nchar(Sys.getenv("token_xxx"))
SAS
%put Token length=%length(%sysget(token_xxx));




R users can alternatively store the REDCap URI and token in the user-level .Renviron file.
Open .Renviron:
usethis::edit_r_environ()
Add the REDCap URI and project token:
redcap_uri="https://redcap.ucdenver.edu/api/"
token_xxx="YOUR_PROJECT_TOKEN"
Restart R after adding or changing values in .Renviron.
The values can then be retrieved without placing credentials in the program:
redcap_uri <- Sys.getenv("redcap_uri")
token <- Sys.getenv("token_xxx")
